name: The Absolute
plain_explanation: Hegel held that individual things -- people, objects, moments in time -- are not fully real or self-sufficient on their own; only the entire interconnected universe, taken as a single organized whole, is truly and completely real. Separate things have only a partial, borrowed reality as aspects of this Whole.
precise_definition: Hegel's term for ultimate reality: a single, complex, organically unified spiritual Whole (not a simple substance, unlike Parmenides' One or Spinoza's God) of which apparently separate finite things are partial, interdependent aspects, fully real and fully understood only in relation to the whole.
why_it_mattered: It is the foundation of Hegel's entire system: his logic, his philosophy of history, and his theory of the State all follow from the claim that reality and truth belong, in the fullest sense, only to the Whole.
historical_origin: Developed across Hegel's Logic and Phenomenology of Mind, rooted in mystical experiences Russell says Hegel had in youth.
examples: The claim that 'nothing is ultimately and completely real except the whole'
The rejection of time and space as fully real, since they involve separateness and multiplicity
objections: Russell's core logical objection: this view depends on the false assumption that any true statement about a part of the universe must be a statement about its relations to everything else, an assumption Russell traces to (and rejects in) traditional subject-predicate logic.
competing_positions: Spinoza's God/Nature, possessing both extension and thought
Analytic philosophy's rejection of holism in favor of genuine, irreducible relations between distinct particulars
influence_on_later_thinkers: Shaped late-nineteenth-century Anglo-American idealism (Bradley, Bosanquet) and, via the dialectic, Marx's materialist reworking of Hegelian history.
connection_to_politics_or_religion: Directly grounds Hegel's later claim that the State, as a more organized whole, has greater reality and value than the individuals who compose it.
